title: Throughput calibration lab notes: thermal-aware priming and client pacing
body:
Summary:

This is an experimental lab notebook for calibrating end-to-end throughput claims while explicitly controlling for thermal hysteresis and client-side pacing effects. The goal is a small, repeatable harness we can run in CI (nightly) and in manual lab runs that gives stable median throughput +/- 2% across runs for a given model and quantization profile.

Motivation/risks observed that motivated this writeup:
- Throughput regressions flake: same config, different day, +/- 8–12% variation.
- Long runs drift down as GPUs thermally throttle; short runs overestimate sustainable throughput.
- Client pacing (poisson vs fixed inter-arrival) changes batching behavior and KV cache occupancy, altering effective token-per-second.
- Seemingly-identical seeds produce different occupancy when background noise (other processes, host CPU load) changes.

High-level approach:
1) Instrument the device and host thermal state; capture power/clock metrics at 1s sampling.
2) Use a deterministic multi-phase warmup that isolates micropriming, occupancy stabilization, and steady-state sampling.
3) Randomize run order and interleave control runs to detect drift/thermal trends.
4) Capture full traces (request/response timestamps, kernel-level perf counters) for post-run attribution.

Testbed (canonical):
- Model: llama-13b-fp16 (reference build date pinned)
- Image: bench-runtime:2026-02-08 (docker image digest pinned)
- GPU: A100-SXM4 80GB (power cap set to 300W unless profiling otherwise)
- Host kernel: ubuntu-22.04 + nvidia-driver 525.116 (note exact kernel module)
- Load generator: bench-client v0.5.2 (sha: a1b2c3)
- Network: isolated lab vlan, <0.5ms hop, clients colocated to avoid external jitter

Metrics to capture:
- End-to-end throughput (tokens/s) aggregated over sliding windows (default 30s windows, 5s step)
- Per-request P95 and P99 latency (ms)
- GPU util, SM clocks, memory clocks, power draw (sampled 1s)
- Kernel counters: L2 hit rate, DRAM read/write counters, Tensor core utilization (where available)
- Batch composition histogram (sizes, prefetched KVs)
- CPU steal/idle/softirq to account for host scheduling noise

Canonical multi-phase warmup (recommended default):
Phase 0 — micropriming (30s): single client, single request with long context to populate KV cache and JIT kernels. Purpose: warm memory and initial kernel caches.
Phase 1 — staircase ramp (6 minutes): 4 stair steps, each 90s: concurrency = [1, 8, 32, target_concurrency/2]. Use fixed inter-arrival in this phase to deterministically fill batching paths.
Phase 2 — occupancy hammer (4 minutes): poisson arrivals with target lambda to create realistic batching variance; clients=N (same as test harness). Purpose: exercise scheduler jitter and check slot-slice behavior.
Phase 3 — settle (2 minutes): reduce to target_concurrency and wait for observed throughput to be within 3% over a 30s sliding window.
Phase 4 — sample (10 minutes): record metrics for analysis. Do not change runtime config during this phase.
Cooldown: 5 minutes idle between runs; if GPU clocks/power not back to baseline, extend to 10 minutes.

Repeatability hygiene checklist:
- Pin docker image digest and model artifact checksum.
- Record kernel versions and nvidia driver + DCGM versions.
- Set GPU power cap and record max clock frequencies; for head-to-head comparisons, run with identical caps.
- Fix CPU governor to performance and pin benchmark process to dedicated cores using taskset.
- Clear page caches and restart bench processes between runs.
- Use rng seed hygiene: record RNG seed, but also randomize run order across seeds to detect seed sensitivity.
- Run 5 independent replicates per bench configuration (randomized order).
- Interleave a short control run (baseline config) every 3 runs to detect drift.

Load generator configuration examples (bench-client format, inline):
{
  "clients": 48,
  "arrival_pattern": "poisson",
  "target_concurrency": 64,
  "seq_length_distribution": "mixed-8-128",
  "seed": 20260214
}

Command-line run example (lab):
CTR=\"a100-80gb-300w\" 
MODEL=llama-13b-fp16 
bench-client run --clients 48 --arrival poisson --seed 20260214 --profile-sample-rate 1s --out run-2026-03-10.json

Observability and traces to collect:
- bench-client traces (per-request timestamps + server side timestamps)
- NVML sampling (nvidia-smi --query-gpu=...) at 1s, logged to CSV
- DCGM telemetry for detailed perf counters if available
- strace of the server process on a single replicate to see syscalls for unexpected blocking
- GPU kernel timeline (nsight or CUPTI) for 1 replicate to map expensive kernels

Post-run analysis steps (scripted):
1) Remove warmup windows (first N seconds as configured).
2) Compute sliding-window throughput series and discard first minute of Phase 4 if trending.
3) Compute median tokens/s, sample variance, CV, and 95% bootstrap CI (1000 resamples).
4) Flag run as anomalous if CV > 5% or if median throughput differs from control by >6%.
5) For significant differences, compare per-window throughput series using a Mann-Whitney U test (report p-value) and plot overlay.

Thermal-specific mitigations and notes:
- If throughput declines monotonically over sampling window and correlates with GPU temperature increase >10C, mark as thermal drift. Consider longer cooldown or active cooling.
- Observe clock throttling events from nvidia-smi; if clocks fall below expected sustained clocks, treat run as invalid for throughput claim.
- For short runs, thermal warmup artifacts can cause overestimation; therefore we require at least 10m sample phase.

Known failure modes and debugging heuristics:
- Symptom: high P99 but good median throughput -> look for rare long requests: inspect request size distribution and batch tailing.
- Symptom: sudden throughput drop mid-sample -> check host CPU steal/softirq and GPU ECC or XID errors.
- Symptom: wide run-to-run variance -> check run order for thermal accumulation, and examine power cap consistency.

Statistical reporting format for PRs/benchmarks:
- Report median tokens/s (bootstrap 95% CI) across replicates and delta vs baseline in percent.
- Include per-run sliding-window plots (transparent overlay), temperature and power time series, and batch-size histogram.
- Include a short note on any excluded runs and reason (thermal, driver error, OOM, other).

Actionable next steps / experiments to schedule:
- Add a short probe to automatically detect and abort runs when clock throttling occurs (avoid wasted runs).
- Implement a CI job that runs the canonical harness once per week with a baseline control and stores artifacts in S3 for longitudinal analysis.
- Evaluate sensitivity of poisson vs fixed inter-arrival on end-to-end throughput variance for conversational vs long-context workloads.
- Prototype active cooling policy for lab rack and measure effect on stability.

Appendix — quick checklist for running a canonical bench:
- [ ] Set power cap to 300W (record).
- [ ] Pull pinned image digest.
- [ ] Run Phase 0..4 as above.
- [ ] Collect NVML CSV, bench trace, DCGM counters, kernel logs.
- [ ] Run analysis script and upload plots + JSON to linked artifacts.

Notes to self: prioritize automating randomization and control interleaving in the harness; manual ordering is a huge source of bias.

End of lab notes.
